name: Electrically Assisted Bicycle
description: A two-wheeled ride whose electric motor can propel it and a 170-pound rider no faster than 20 mph on a paved, level surface. Montana has no class 1/2/3 system: the definition counts it as a bicycle, so it rides under bicycle law.

restrictions.rule: Two tandem wheels and an electric motor; the definition draws no line between a throttle and pedal assist (Montana Code Annotated §61-8-102(7))
The motor can't propel it and a 170-pound rider faster than 20 mph on a paved, level surface (Montana Code Annotated §61-8-102(7))
No motor wattage limit in the definition (Montana Code Annotated §61-8-102(7))
No classes: a 28 mph pedal-assist (class 3) e-bike fails the 20 mph test and isn't an electrically assisted bicycle (Montana Code Annotated §61-8-102(7))
A faster machine with pedals, a power source of at most 2 brake horsepower and a top speed of 30 mph is a moped instead (Montana Code Annotated §61-8-102(14))
Counts as a bicycle under state law, with a bicycle's rights and duties (Montana Code Annotated §61-8-102(2))
No driver's license, registration or insurance
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed; federal land managers may still treat it as motorized on their trails
